title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-07-08
content:
TL;DR:
- Kernel scheduling fixes merged to canary; expect 5-8% p99 latency improvement for 8k+ contexts.
- KV-cache: prototype eviction policy (LRU-window) shows 18% reduction in avg token compute on chat workload; still seeing edge-case thrash on multi-session tails.
- Batching: adaptive-batcher rollout paused after regression on mixed-length workloads (see INF-4680).

This week summary:
- Kernel work:
  - Merged kernel scheduling improvements (PR #1287). Changes: better co-scheduling of small-token requests to avoid underutilized SMs; adjust warp occupancy heuristics for attention kernels.
  - Benchmark: internal canary on p4d with Llama2-70B quantized profile. End-to-end p99 improved from 380ms -> 350ms on long-context chat (12k tokens). Throughput at 95th percentile unchanged.
  - Next step: push optimized schedule to dedicated staging for wider workload exerciser next week.

- KV cache updates:
  - Prototype eviction (LRU-window) implemented in kv-cache service. Tracks per-session recency windows to avoid evicting hot prefixes used across short-lived parallel sessions.
  - Offline sim on production traces (last 2 weeks): avg per-token compute down ~18% for chat-heavy users; tail sessions with rapid topic switches still generate thrash.
  - Instrumentation added: per-session hit-rate histograms, hot-prefix heatmaps, and eviction churn metric. Dashboard link in Confluence.
  - Blocker: interaction with prefix-caching + persistence layer has a race under GC path that can cause double-alloc of slot ids (INF-4621). Hotfix branch created; tests failing in CI under heavy concurrency.

- Batching and scheduler:
  - Adaptive-batcher (size + latency-aware) initial rollout to 10% of traffic. Observed favorable improvements on uniform-length request streams (~12% token/sec improvement), but regression on mixed-length (short+very-long) where short requests saw higher p50 latency.
  - Root cause: scheduler starving small requests while waiting for long requests to complete the KV fetch; need to introduce size-based prioritization threshold.
  - Action: rollback to 0% rollout for now. Plan: implement and test prioritization policy (work item INF-4680).

Metrics highlights (canary vs prod baseline):
- p99 latency (12k context): canary 350ms vs baseline 380ms (8% improvement)
- avg token compute (chat traces): prototype kv-cache -18%
- request-level p50 for short requests (<=128 tokens): +15% on adaptive-batcher subset (regression)

Standup notes (2026-07-08):
- Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Jasmin, Liam, Priya
- Ethan: kernel schedule merged; pushing staging job tonight. Asked for additional microbench for memory bandwidth.
- Jasmin: KV eviction prototype working but hitting race in GC path. Will pair with Priya on hotfix.
- Liam: batching rollback executed. Will write spec for prioritization threshold; wants ops to reproduce mixed-workload pattern.
- Priya: added dashboards + alerts for eviction churn. Noticed correlation between churn spikes and a particular client (client-id: corp-acct-42). Opening CS ticket to ask for workload patterns.

Open blockers / risks:
- INF-4621: KV cache GC race -> hotfix blocked on reproducer. High priority.
- INF-4680: Batcher prioritization spec and test harness needed. Without it cannot progress rollout.
- Resource: need another GPU node in dedicated staging for wider kernel stress tests; ops queued (~3 day lead).

Decisions made:
- Rollback adaptive-batcher rollout until prioritization policy is implemented and validated.
- Prioritize KV GC race fix over incremental optimizations; aim to have repro & fix in this sprint.

Action items (owner - due):
- Maya: coordinate with SRE to get extra staging node for kernel tests - due 2026-07-12.
- Ethan: run memory-bandwidth microbench and post results - due 2026-07-09.
- Jasmin & Priya: reproduce GC race locally and push hotfix PR - due 2026-07-10.
- Liam: draft batching prioritization spec + test harness example traces - due 2026-07-11.
- Data team (asked): provide 48h production trace subset focusing on chat sessions for KV sims - requested; due 2026-07-09.

Meeting log / notes:
- Kernel sync (2026-07-07): Discussed occupancy heuristics and fallback for very small batch sizes. Agreement: if observed SM utilization < 20% and queue length < 4, switch to eager-mode to reduce p50. Follow-up: Ethan to prototype.
- KV design review (2026-07-06): Reviewed eviction policy variants. Decision: use LRU-window as primary + per-prefix hot flags; fallback to frequency-based evict only when churn > threshold. Jasmin to add tests.
- Batching retrospective (2026-07-05): Collected logs from rollout. Noted skewed client distribution causing more mixed-length cases than expected; Ops to provide sample client traces.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add more visibility for per-model quantization impacts in kernel benchmarks.
- Consider per-tenant KV cache sizing policy (follow-up with product).
- Keep canary for kernel changes small but run longer to catch tail interactions with cache.

References / links:
- INF-4621 (KV GC race) -> jira ticket
- INF-4680 (Batcher prioritization) -> jira ticket
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1287
- Confluence: /pages/serving-runtime-kv-cache-design
summary: Weekly update covering kernel scheduling improvements (merged), KV-cache prototype with eviction policy and instrumentation, adaptive-batcher rollback and next steps, blockers INF-4621 & INF-4680, action items assigned.
